concepts.definition: The inherent inability of natural language to fully specify meaning without contextual grounding; includes word-sense ambiguity, referential ambiguity, and scope ambiguity that conversational systems struggle to resolve without visual or structural context.
key_refs: Dealing with Semantic Underspecification in Multimodal NLP (ACL 2023)
Semantic Underspecification - Language and Linguistics Compass (2010)
Disambiguation in Conversational Question Answering in the Era of LLM (2025)
concepts.implication: MetroGraph must complement conversational querying with visual node/edge representations that ground semantic meaning; pure text cannot fully specify graph structures or query intent without spatial scaffolding.

concepts.definition: The progressive loss or unavailability of sufficient contextual information across dialogue turns, causing systems to misunderstand user intent due to missing pronoun resolution, implicit references, or unstated assumptions.
key_refs: Conversational Information Seeking (2022)
A Survey of Conversational Search (2024)
Towards Universal Dialogue State Tracking (2018)
concepts.implication: MetroGraph must make query context (selected nodes, filters, scope) visually persistent; temporal linear dialogue cannot reliably maintain structured state that users expect to persist across interaction.

concepts.concept: Intent Recognition Failure in Complex Dialogue
concepts.definition: The inability of conversational systems to accurately classify user intents from natural language utterances, especially when users express multiple simultaneous goals, have out-of-distribution phrasings, or rely on conversational implicature.
key_refs: Intent Recognition in Dialogue Systems (2024)
Multi-Intent Recognition in Dialogue Understanding (2024)
Dialogue Agents 101: Critical Ingredients for Designing Effective Conversational Systems (2023)
concepts.implication: MetroGraph must provide visual intent specification (drag nodes, set constraints, compose operators) rather than relying on NLU; explicit structural inputs are more reliable than natural language for graph manipulation.

concepts.definition: The systematic failure of conversational systems to employ human-expected repair and clarification strategies when misunderstanding occurs; systems lack the contextual models and cooperative principles that humans use to recover from dialogue breakdowns.
key_refs: An analysis of dialogue repair in virtual assistants (2024)
System and User Strategies to Repair Conversational Breakdowns (2024)
Exploring human error recovery strategies: Implications for spoken dialogue systems (2005)
Clarification in Spoken Dialogue Systems (2003)
concepts.implication: MetroGraph should provide immediate visual feedback (highlighting selections, showing query results) to surface misunderstandings before requiring verbal repair; proactive error prevention through UI feedback reduces reliance on conversational error recovery.

concepts.definition: The inability of conversational systems to infer speaker intent from conversational implicature, context-dependent meaning, and cooperative principles (Grice); systems fail to understand what is meant versus what is literally said.
key_refs: Expanding the Set of Pragmatic Considerations in Conversational AI (2023)
Implicature in Interaction: Understanding Implicature Improves Alignment in Human-LLM Interaction (2024)
Towards an Analysis of Discourse and Interactional Pragmatic Reasoning Capabilities of Large Language Models (2024)
concepts.implication: MetroGraph must use explicit structural affordances (node colors, layout, annotations) to communicate system intent instead of relying on conversational implicature; visual grammar is less ambiguous than natural language pragmatics.

concepts.definition: The core architectural limitation where systems must maintain and update a consistent belief state about dialogue context across turns; heterogeneous dialogue representations, domain-specific state schemas, and cross-domain generalization failures prevent robust state maintenance.
key_refs: Dialogue State Tracking in Task-Oriented Systems (2023)
Towards Universal Dialogue State Tracking (2018)
Evaluating LLM-based Agents for Multi-Turn Conversations: A Survey (2025)
concepts.implication: MetroGraph must make graph state visually persistent through a spatial canvas instead of maintaining hidden dialogue state; explicit visual representation of nodes/edges/filters eliminates the need for context tracking across interaction turns.

concepts.concept: Constraint Discovery Problem in Conversational Interfaces
concepts.definition: Users cannot discover system capabilities, constraints, or valid input ranges through natural conversation; conversational interfaces lack affordances for revealing what is possible, leading to abandonmentin when phrasing differs from system expectations.
key_refs: Chat Failures and Troubles: Reasons and Solutions (2023)
Convo: What does conversational programming need? An exploration of machine learning interface design (2020)
The Conversation Trap: why defaulting to chat might be the biggest interaction design mistake of the AI era (2026)
concepts.implication: MetroGraph must surface operators, filters, and valid query patterns through visual UI elements (menus, drag-drop controls, schema visualization) rather than relying on users to discover them through trial-and-error conversation.

concepts.definition: Persistent disconnect between users' mental models of what a conversational system can do and its actual capabilities; transparency features paradoxically reduce satisfaction and do not bridge the comprehension gap.
key_refs: Exploring users' mental models of conversational agents: a systematic review (2025)
Understanding Mental Models of Generative Conversational Search and The Effect of Interface Transparency (2025)
Transparent Conversational Agents: The Impact of Capability Communication on User Behavior and Mental Model Alignment (2024)
concepts.implication: MetroGraph must use visual system metaphors (graph, schema, data structures) that align with how users conceptually think about structured data; design interface to match user mental models of the problem domain rather than trying to explain system internals.

concepts.definition: Natural language alone is insufficient for specifying complex visual or structural tasks (visualization, layout, graph operations); unimodal text-only intent is inadequately grounded in spatial or visual context.
key_refs: Towards Natural Language Interfaces for Data Visualization: A Survey (2021)
Deep Learning Approaches for Multimodal Intent Recognition: A Survey (2024)
Show, Don't Tell: Reflections on the Design of Multi-modal Conversational Interfaces (2021)
concepts.implication: MetroGraph inherently requires multimodal interaction: conversational queries must be paired with visual node selection, spatial layout, and structural constraints. Graph visualization is not optional scaffolding but essential specification mechanism.

concepts.definition: Sequential turn-taking in conversational interfaces constrains exploration and multi-path reasoning; linear chat history cannot represent parallel hypotheses, branching decision trees, or non-sequential task flows that users need for complex work.
key_refs: ChatGraPhT: A Visual Conversation Interface for Multi-Path Reflection with Agentic LLM Support (2024)
Do Conversational Interfaces Limit Creativity? Exploring Visual Graph Systems for Creative Writing (2024)
Agentic Workflows for Conversational Human-AI Interaction Design (2025)
concepts.implication: MetroGraph's graph-based interface directly addresses this by representing multiple query paths, branching logic, and parallel explorations as spatial structures; graph canvas enables non-linear, exploratory interaction that linear chat cannot support.

concepts.definition: The tendency of large language models in extended conversations to repeat prior decisions or become locked into early dialogue patterns despite receiving longer context; extended context does not monotonically improve multi-turn dialogue quality.
key_refs: Mitigating Conversational Inertia in Multi-Turn Agents (2025)
concepts.implication: MetroGraph avoids dialogue inertia by using explicit visual state representation (nodes, edges, filters) that users can directly manipulate; visual representation prevents the model from being locked into prior conversational patterns.

concepts.definition: Conversational AI systems generate plausible-sounding but factually false information (hallucinations); grounding to external data is insufficient, and architectural constraints are needed to ensure conversational truthfulness in constrained domains.
key_refs: Mitigating LLM Hallucinations Using a Multi-Agent Framework (2024)
Context Window Limits: Why Your LLM Still Hallucinates (2026)
concepts.implication: MetroGraph must enforce constraints at the interface level (valid operators, schema-constrained queries, real-time result feedback) to prevent hallucinated results; conversational query must be validated against actual graph structure before execution.

concepts.concept: Query Reformulation Failure in Conversational RAG
concepts.definition: Automatic query rewriting in conversational RAG systems fails to capture user intent from conversational context, particularly for co-reference resolution and context-dependent pronoun binding.
key_refs: Can Synthetic Query Rewrites Capture User Intent Better than Humans in Retrieval-Augmented Generation? (2024)
Beyond Pipelines: A Fundamental Study on the Rise of Generative-Retrieval Architectures in Web Research (2025)
concepts.implication: MetroGraph should allow users to explicitly specify query context through visual graph annotations (selected nodes, constraints) rather than relying on conversational query reformulation to infer intent from chat history.

concepts.definition: Dialogue systems can complete tasks accurately but still produce low user satisfaction; task completion rate and dialogue efficiency are independent of user experience quality, indicating systems miss critical UX dimensions.
key_refs: Understanding User Satisfaction with Task-oriented Dialogue Systems (2022)
Assessing Interaction Quality in Human–AI Dialogue: An Integrative Review and Multi-Layer Framework for Conversational Agents (2023)
How to Evaluate Your Dialogue Models: A Review of Approaches (2021)
concepts.implication: MetroGraph must prioritize user agency, comprehension, and feedback loops alongside task completion; visual interface transparency that shows query structure, constraints, and results helps close the satisfaction gap.

concepts.concept: Direct Manipulation Superiority for Regularly-Used Tasks
concepts.definition: Foundational HCI principle that direct manipulation interfaces outperform conversational interfaces for routine, well-understood tasks; spatial, reversible, visually-encoded actions provide superior cognitive efficiency and user control.
key_refs: Direct Manipulation Interfaces (Norman, 1983)
Designing the User Interface: Strategies for Effective Human-Computer Interaction (Shneiderman, 2016)
Shneiderman's Eight Golden Rules of Interface Design (1987)
Conversational agent or direct manipulation in human–system interaction (2005)
concepts.implication: MetroGraph embraces direct manipulation (drag nodes, draw edges, apply filters spatially) for database graph queries because users perform these queries repeatedly; direct manipulation outperforms conversation for this task class.

concepts.definition: Human information-seeking involves iterative exploration guided by information scent (Pirolli); conversations alone cannot provide the visual cues and interactive feedback that guide exploration, requiring navigation through information landscape.
key_refs: Information Seeking Behavior - an overview (Pirolli's Information Foraging Theory, 2000s)
concepts.implication: MetroGraph's graph visualization provides visual scent (node colors, edge patterns, result previews) that guides users through query exploration; conversational interfaces lack the ambient information cues needed for foraging behavior.

concepts.definition: Conversational interfaces provide no affordances for discovering available operations, constraints, or valid parameter ranges; users must resort to trial-and-error or explicit help-seeking rather than visual hints.
key_refs: The Conversation Trap: why defaulting to chat might be the biggest interaction design mistake of the AI era (2026)
Beyond the Conversation Trap: Designing for Hybrid Human-Agent Interaction Modes (2026)
concepts.implication: MetroGraph surfaces query capabilities through UI elements (visible operators, type hints, schema visualization) rather than forcing users to discover them conversationally; visual affordances enable passive learning and rapid capability discovery.

concepts.definition: Brief, transient nature of conversational turns limits opportunities for sustained user engagement; interactions are ephemeral without persistent visualization of interaction history and context.
key_refs: Agentic Workflows for Conversational Human-AI Interaction Design (2025)
concepts.implication: MetroGraph provides persistent visual canvas where query structures, results, and refinements remain visible and replayable; spatial persistence addresses the transience problem by making interaction artifacts durable.

concepts.definition: Wide range of conversational AI capabilities combined with unlimited possible user goals creates a vast ambiguous design space; users cannot easily constrain their requests to valid system functionality.
key_refs: Agentic Workflows for Conversational Human-AI Interaction Design (2025)
concepts.implication: MetroGraph constrains the design space by providing domain-specific visual operators for graph queries (node filters, edge traversals, aggregations); explicit constraints in the UI reduce ambiguity compared to open-ended natural language.

concepts.concept: Web Interface Control Failure with Pure Language
concepts.definition: LLMs controlling web interfaces through language instructions fail for visual/spatial tasks and structural navigation requiring real-time visual feedback and iterative refinement.
key_refs: WebWISE: Web Interface Control and Sequential Exploration with Large Language Models (2023)
concepts.implication: MetroGraph must maintain visual feedback loops (showing node selections, query previews, result highlights) because pure language instructions cannot reliably specify complex structural manipulations.

concepts.definition: Coordination and complexity issues emerge when multiple conversational agents operate together; chat paradigm does not scale to multi-agent scenarios requiring orchestration and role clarity.
key_refs: One Agent Too Many: User Perspectives on Approaches to Multi-agent Conversational AI (2024)
concepts.implication: MetroGraph's node-based graph model naturally supports multi-agent scenarios through visual role differentiation (node types, coloring, annotations); graph structure makes agent roles and interactions explicit.

concepts.concept: Cognitive Load of Linear Chat for Structured Tasks
concepts.definition: Conversational interfaces impose high cognitive load for structured data tasks by forcing users to maintain mental models of invisible system state, remember prior context, and reconcile linear dialogue with non-linear task logic.
key_refs: Visualization Analysis and Design (Munzner, 2014)
Designing the User Interface: Strategies for Effective Human-Computer Interaction (Shneiderman, 2016)
Conversational User Interfaces for Blind Knowledge Workers: A Case Study (2020)
concepts.implication: MetroGraph reduces cognitive load by externalizing query structure as visual graph: nodes represent entities, edges show relationships, visual constraints are spatially encoded. External representation reduces working memory demand.

concepts.concept: NL Interface Ambiguity for Structured Tasks
concepts.definition: Natural language interfaces for structured tasks (NL2VIS, NL2SQL, NL2Query) fail due to ambiguity in visual specification, context maintenance, and lack of affordances for constraint expression.
key_refs: Towards Natural Language Interfaces for Data Visualization: A Survey (2021)
concepts.implication: MetroGraph augments NL with visual graph semantics: structured queries are specified through direct manipulation (selecting nodes, composing operators visually), reducing ambiguity compared to pure NL approaches.

concepts.definition: Transparency features and explanations alone are insufficient for helping users calibrate trust in AI systems; users need to understand system boundaries, confidence limits, and failure modes beyond capability descriptions.
key_refs: Trust Calibration in Agentic AI: Designing for Appropriate Reliance, Not Blind Trust (2026)
concepts.implication: MetroGraph must design interfaces that make query semantics and execution bounds transparent (showing exactly which nodes match, what constraints apply) rather than relying on conversational explanations of AI behavior.

concepts.concept: Semantic Grounding Failure in Multi-Agent NL Interfaces
concepts.definition: Natural language interfaces for multi-agent task assignment fail due to semantic grounding challenges when mapping NL to workflows; explicit constraints are necessary to disambiguate intent.
key_refs: Towards A Natural Language Interface for Flexible Multi-Agent Task Assignment (2023)
concepts.implication: MetroGraph's graph structure provides semantic grounding for multi-query workflows: visual node composition, edge constraints, and type annotations make assignment semantics explicit without NL ambiguity.

concepts.definition: Systems struggle to maintain coherent dialogue and generate contextually appropriate responses; automatic metrics cannot capture true interaction quality beyond task completion.
key_refs: How to Evaluate Your Dialogue Models: A Review of Approaches (2021)
Survey on Evaluation Methods for Dialogue Systems (2019)
concepts.implication: MetroGraph avoids dialogue coherence problems by using explicit visual protocol (graph state, query structure) that both user and system maintain synchronously; no hidden dialogue state to maintain.

concepts.concept: Survey Consensus on Multi-User CUI Challenges
concepts.definition: Systematic reviews document persistent design challenges in conversational interfaces: context management, turn-taking ambiguity, and architectural complexity that remain unsolved across implementations.
key_refs: A Survey on Multi-User Conversational Interfaces (2024)
concepts.implication: MetroGraph's approach of combining graph visualization with optional conversational layer acknowledges these persistent challenges by not relying on conversation alone for structured queries.

concepts.definition: Conversational systems fail to effectively communicate what capabilities they do and do not have; users struggle with invisible constraints until they encounter failures.
key_refs: Convo: What does conversational programming need? An exploration of machine learning interface design (2020)
concepts.implication: MetroGraph makes capabilities explicit through UI schema (visible operators, type constraints, available node types) rather than requiring conversational discovery of what is possible.
